idiom_name: spool directory with os.File.Sync + rename, drained by one goroutine
implementation_notes: The standard library supplies the pieces but not the queue: create the spool file with os.CreateTemp in the spool directory, write, call File.Sync() to force the data to stable storage, close, then os.Rename it into place - the os package documents that Rename is not an atomic operation on non-Unix platforms, so the spool directory is a local detail to be kept consistent. A single goroutine drains in name order and removes the file only after the peer acknowledged, with context.Context carrying cancellation and exponential backoff between attempts. Reaching for a broker only moves durability to the broker: kafka-go's Writer buffers in memory and RequiredAcks=kafka.RequireAll confirms the hop, not a local store.
pitfalls: Forgetting File.Sync(): the bytes stay in the page cache, so a machine crash loses accepted messages even though Write returned nil.
Both os.Rename across filesystems (EXDEV) and a temp file created outside the spool directory defeat the atomic-appearance assumption.
os.Remove before the acknowledgement - or in a defer that also runs on the failure path - drops the message on the first transport error.
Writer and drainer must agree on the spool file naming/ordering scheme; second-granularity timestamps collide and scramble drain order.
